title: SOLID design
rule: Use SOLID principles in production code design.
why: Keeps responsibilities focused and dependencies understandable, so changes remain localized as the codebase evolves.

title: Clean Code
rule: Apply Clean Code principles in production and test code.
why: Keeps code readable and intention-revealing, preventing avoidable maintenance mistakes.

title: Unit-test coverage floor
rule: Maintain unit-test code coverage of at least 65%.
why: Prevents the core behaviour from becoming unverified as the server evolves.

name: Resolved store snapshot
problem: Append-only FluencyLoop records need one deterministic current view without hiding malformed or unfamiliar local evidence.
how: The reader discovers sorted JSONL files, reads each line independently, replaces supported identities with their newest record, and returns unkeyed records and diagnostics alongside the resolved state.
tags:
append-only log
read model
event sourcing

title: Resilient local inspection
rule: Preserve valid local evidence and report damaged input as diagnostics; do not fail the whole inspection because one local record is malformed.
why: Prevents one damaged JSONL line from hiding the remaining repository evidence.

name: Root-confined repository snapshot
problem: Repository inspection must not expose paths outside the supplied root, while callers still need regular-file and Git-tracking state.
how: The observer canonicalizes the root, skips .git, excludes symbolic links, sorts root-relative files, and attaches tracking diagnostics when Git cannot report state.
tags:
filesystem boundary
repository snapshot
defensive traversal

name: Deterministic evidence drift
problem: Recorded source-path evidence needs stable, honest findings when files are missing, not tracked, or outside the repository root.
how: The analyzer extracts resolved concept evidence, validates relative paths, compares them with the repository snapshot, sorts findings, and marks reports incomplete when tracking data is unavailable.
tags:
drift detection
deterministic output
read model

title: Root-confined repository inspection
rule: Observe only regular, non-symbolic-link files below the supplied canonical repository root, and exclude Git metadata.
why: Prevents repository inspection from following a path outside the requested boundary.

name: Comparison service
problem: MCP handlers need one read-only application boundary that combines store, repository, and drift work without embedding comparison rules in transport code.
how: ComparisonService delegates to the existing store reader, repository observer, and drift analyzer, then returns JSON-compatible results to the MCP adapter.

name: MCP stdio boundary
problem: Clients need exactly three schema-validated read-only tools without protocol details leaking into comparison logic.
how: McpServerFactory registers get_store_snapshot, get_repository_snapshot, and check_drift with repository_root schemas on the official synchronous SDK stdio transport.
tags:
MCP server
stdio transport
adapter pattern

name: Runnable MCP distribution
problem: A local MCP server must run as the same packaged artifact that automated verification exercises.
how: Maven attaches a shaded executable JAR and Failsafe launches it for an initialize, tool listing, and tool call exchange over standard streams.
tags:
executable artifact
integration testing
protocol verification

title: SDK-owned protocol handling
rule: Use the official MCP SDK for protocol framing, transport behavior, and tool-schema validation; keep application code focused on product operations.
why: Prevents local server code from duplicating or drifting from the MCP protocol.
